- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.27) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 73), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3–5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.77) and price is trending up, model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 1–3% to avoid overconfidence in momentum.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon; if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.27–0.53), model tends to lag; forecast should be adjusted to align with 3-day moving average of true values, not just historical trend.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early downward momentum; if true outcome shows 2+ consecutive drops >5% from peak, reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 3 days.
